sources.entry: Actual - Local-first personal finance tool based on zero-sum budgeting, supporting synchronization across devices, custom rules, manual transaction importing (from QIF, OFX, and QFX files), and optional automatic synchronization with many banks. (Source Code) MIT Nodejs/Docker
Actual Budget | Local-first personal finance and envelope budgeting app

summary.one_liner: Actual is a free, open-source, local-first personal finance and envelope/zero-sum budgeting app written in NodeJS, with cross-device sync.
summary.what_it_does: Actual is a local-first personal finance tool written in NodeJS, described as 100% free and open-source. It includes a synchronization element so changes move between devices. The README names four deployment options: PikaPods one-click hosting, Fly.io managed hosting, self-hosting with a Docker image, and downloadable Windows, Mac and Linux local-only apps. The app is organized into packages: loot-core (core logic for any platform), desktop-client (desktop UI), and desktop-electron (desktop app). The README points to community documentation for budgeting, account management, and tips, plus migration and "starting fresh" guides for users coming from other budgeting apps. The awesome-selfhosted listing adds that it supports custom rules, manual import of QIF, OFX and QFX files, and optional automatic sync with many banks; these details come from the listing metadata, not the README.
use_cases: self-hosting a finance app with Docker
importing bank statements from QIF, OFX or QFX files
how_to_run: Self-host using the Docker image (see installation docs)
Download the Windows, Mac or Linux local-only desktop app
notable: Local-first design with optional multi-device synchronization
Multiple deployment options including local-only desktop apps
Imports QIF, OFX and QFX files; optional automatic bank sync (per listing metadata)
caveats: Hosted options (PikaPods, Fly.io) carry monthly fees
Automatic bank synchronization is optional and not described in the README itself
Self-hosting requires running Docker or Node setup (installation docs linked, not detailed here)
